$purpose: First-class places list for FRQNCY — physical venues where practices happen. Retreats, sanctuaries, spaces, future FRQNCY venues.
$source: Seeded from explore.html (places block) + /places/<slug>/index.html pages. Covers Intaaya, Essência, plus 7 sweep entries (Auroville, Esalen, Findhorn, Monroe Institute, Plum Village, Schumacher College, Tassajara) backfilled 2026-05-12 from existing /places/ pages and explore-data.json edges.
$id_prefix: pl- (places) to avoid collision with p- (people), b- (books), o- (orgs), m- (media). The older explore.html uses p- for places; that legacy reference will be migrated in a follow-up pass.

$schema.name: Canonical place name
$schema.bio: One-paragraph description in the FRQNCY voice
$schema.appears_in: Array of topic/domain/pillar ids where this place should appear on the site
$schema.picked_in: Array of bucket ids where the place gets the ✦ FRQNCY PICK badge
$schema.teachers_in_residence: (optional) Array of p-ids — linking humans who teach at this place
$schema.practices: (optional) Array of topic slugs describing what the place hosts — currently implicit via appears_in

places.name: Intaaya
places.bio: Regenerative retreat sanctuary on Nusa Penida, near Bali. Off-grid, farm-to-table, living to the rhythm of nature. A living example of the Sanctuary pillar — the physical extension of the FRQNCY network.

places.name: Essência
places.bio: An off-grid regenerative eco-village and whole-person healing center on the wild Atlantic coast of southern Portugal. Essência runs as an intentional community curating retreats, courses, and a Healing Center alongside daily life — a natural laboratory for self-exploration, individual realisation, and collective healing. Sustainable living, ecovillage practice, and community living shown as one continuous discipline rather than three separate trends.

places.name: Auroville
places.bio: A universal city in southern India, founded 1968 to embody human unity. Inspired by Sri Aurobindo and The Mother, endorsed by UNESCO. A half-century-long experiment in voluntary, post-national community — where the network-state question is already a built environment, not a thesis.

places.name: Esalen Institute
places.bio: Founded 1962 on the cliffs of Big Sur. The hub of the human potential movement — where Gestalt, somatics, encounter groups, and east-meets-west consciousness work were forged. Hot springs, workshops, retreats. Much of the modern wellness vocabulary was first written down here.

places.name: Findhorn Foundation
places.bio: A spiritual community and ecovillage on the Scottish coast, founded 1962. Famed for the early gardens grown 'in cooperation with the intelligence of nature,' now a working model of regenerative living — half a century of evidence that ecovillage practice is a long game, not a season.

places.name: The Monroe Institute
places.bio: Founded 1971 in the Blue Ridge foothills of Virginia. The world's leading institute for structured exploration of consciousness — home of Hemi-Sync audio technology and the Gateway Voyage program. States beyond ordinary waking taught as skills, not visited as accidents.

places.name: Plum Village
places.bio: Thich Nhat Hanh's mindfulness practice centre, founded 1982 in the south of France. The home of Engaged Buddhism in the West — slow walks, silent meals, the bell of mindfulness pulling attention back to the body across an afternoon.

places.name: Schumacher College
places.bio: A learning centre founded 1990 on the Dartington estate in Devon. Named for E.F. Schumacher, author of Small Is Beautiful. Ecology, systems thinking, regenerative economics — taught with hands in the soil and a curriculum that treats head and body as one instrument.

places.name: Tassajara Zen Mountain Center
places.bio: The first Zen Buddhist monastery established in the West, founded 1967 in a remote Big Sur canyon. Hot springs, silence, traditional Soto Zen training. Home of the Tassajara Bread Book — and proof that monastic form translates without losing what made it work in the original.

places.name: Merlin's
places.bio: Immersive dining in Ubud, Bali — the food chooses you, through tarot cards and divine numerology. The menu is selected for each guest by the cards drawn at the table. A FRQNCY-aligned restaurant where eating becomes ceremony, not transaction.

places.name: Yogaville
places.bio: Satchidananda Ashram, founded in 1980 by Sri Swami Satchidananda — the swami who opened Woodstock. Integral Yoga community on 750 acres along the James River, with the LOTUS shrine at its centre: a temple to all faiths. Retreats, immersions, daily satsang. The clearest American expression of integral, all-paths spirituality as a lived practice.
